While at anchor, the crew was preparing to heave up the anchor when crew members observed footprints leading from the forward hawse pipe.

An immediate search of the vessel was conducted, during which several items were found missing from the forecastle area, including fire hose couplings and scupper plugs.

A subsequent review of the vessel's CCTV footage confirmed that two perpetrators armed with knives had boarded the vessel. The crew members were not injured.

While at anchor, duty crew on board noticed a small wooden boat alongside the ship and four perpetrators on the aft deck. The alarm was raised, resulting in the perpetrators escaping with stolen engine spares.

The incident was reported to port control and the local agent.

While at berth, three perpetrators approached the ship's hull from the sea using a motorboat and boarded the ship. The crew later discovered eight reefer cables were stolen.

The Indonesian Navy Regional Command (Kodaeral) I Quick Response Team (QRT), together with the BNCT security team, investigated the incident.

While being towed by the tug boat Eng Hup Terra, the Master of the tug boat observed an unauthorized boat alongside the vessel. The Master immediately ceased towing operations and manoeuvred the tug boat back towards the vessel to investigate. The crew boarded the work vessel approximately 15 minutes later, by which the unauthorised boat had departed the area. Further inspection revealed that several items were missing, including the emergency fire pump and a portable air compressor. There were no crew onboard at the time of the incident.

The incident was immediately reported to Singapore Vessel Traffic Information System (VTIS) (flag State).

While the vessel was loading palm kernel shells at berth, the watch helmsman discovered two perpetrators rummaging through the spare parts room in the engine room. The watch helmsman immediately made an emergency call to the ship. The perpetrators fled towards the wheelhouse and jumped overboard from the stern deck upon being noticed. They escaped via a small boat waiting nearby. The crew then conducted a search on board. Some spare parts of the generator were stolen. The crew were not injured. 

The incident was reported to Polairud Marine Police. The Marine Police carried out information gathering on the ship.

While at anchor, at least one perpetrator boarded the ship through freeboard on port bow and went to the paint store at forecastle. A thorough search was conducted on board. 75 cans of paints and a set of cables for welding machines were stolen. The crew were not injured. 

The incident was reported to the local agent and Vung Tau Border Defence Force.

While berthed, the vessel’s shore security watchman and duty crew detected three to four perpetrators near the port-side midship store. The alarm was immediately raised, alerting the crew and security personnel. Upon activation of the ship’s alarm, the perpetrators escaped. A search was conducted and ship stores, including an emergency hydraulic hand pump, hydraulic blowers and spare PV valves, were stolen from the midship store. Investigation revealed the perpetrators gained access to the vessel from the seaside using hooks and ropes, and subsequently forced entry into the locked midship store. The crew was not injured.

The Bangladesh Coast Guard (BCG) subsequently boarded the vessel to conduct further investigation.

While anchored, two perpetrators wearing T-shirts and shorts boarded the ship from a small boat using a rope and hook via the poop deck port quarter. The alarm was raised and the perpetrators escaped with stolen engine store spares. The crew was not injured.

While the vessel was transiting the Malacca Strait prior to its arrival in Singapore, the third Engineer discovered that the spare store had been disturbed and immediately reported the incident to the Chief Engineer. A subsequent inventory check confirmed that two turbocharger service kits, two main bearing metal assemblies, one crankpin bearing metal, and one piston ring set were missing. All crew members were accounted for and safe.

The incident was reported to the flag State.

While anchored, during routine safety rounds, the duty AB discovered that perpetrators boarded the vessel. The crew conducted a thorough search of the vessel. However, no perpetrators were found onboard. Subsequent onboard checks revealed that several items were stolen from the bosun store, including a brass bell, electrical wires and cables, butterfly nuts, stools, a chain locker sounding cap, a sounding pipe, and a hydraulic oil refilling cap. All crew members were safe and accounted for.

The Master reported the incident through the local agent to the local Port Authority.

While underway, a group of perpetrators boarded the vessel and stole ship stores. As this was a vessel to be scrapped, there was no security staff or watchmen onboard.

The ship's local agent informed Bangladesh Coast Guard (BCG) and Chittagong Port Authority. BCG sent a boarding party to the vessel and conducted an investigation onboard. BCG and River Police subsequently recovered and handed over the stolen items to concern authority and shipping agent.

While underway, five perpetrators armed with a knife and a gun-like object were sighted in the engine room. Ship's general alarm was activated, deck lights switched on and all crew mustered. A search was conducted with no further sighting of the perpetrators onboard. All crew were accounted for and were safe. Some engine spares were stolen.

Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN) and Singapore Police Coast Guard (SPCG) were notified of the incident. SPCG boarded the vessel and conducted a security search. No perpetrators were found on board. Information was shared with the Indonesia authorities.

While anchored, the duty officer onboard noticed several small boats near the forward of the vessel and notified the bosun to check. After several minutes, on not receiving any response from the bosun, the duty officer raised the alarm. Crew mustered and proceeded to the forecastle where they saw the bosun tied up. Seven perpetrators carrying knives were also seen escaping from the forecastle store. On investigating, ship properties were reported as stolen. The incident was reported to Belawan VTS, Coast Guard and the local agent.
While underway, the barge was boarded by three perpetrators. Four lashing wires, eight turn buckles, one solar light and 10 shovels were stolen. The crew on the tugboat were not injured.

While anchored, four perpetrators armed with knives/bladed weapons boarded the vessel by climbing a rope attached to the forecastle area. Upon boarding, the perpetrators proceeded to the bosun store and forcibly opened the door. After the incident was discovered, the crew immediately secured the area and activated the alarm. Some ship property/stores were stolen.

The incident was reported to Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) Manila and Coast Guard Station (CGS) Manila. Upon receiving the report, Coast Guard Sub-Station (CGSS) North Harbor and CGS Manila personnel, together with Investigation Detection Unit (IDU) personnel carried out investigation.

While underway, four perpetrators were sighted in the engine room. One of the perpetrators carried a gun-like object and three perpetrators were unarmed. The Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) Corregidor of Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) coordinated with Coast Guard Sub Station (CGSS) North Harbor on the incident. Upon receiving the information, personnel of the substation immediately proceeded to CGSS Navotas to assist the Investigation and Detection Unit (IDU) personnel conducting the investigation and communicating with the Master of the vessel.

A subsequent search confirmed no perpetrators remained onboard, but 2900 litres of assorted paint were stolen. The crew were not injured.

While at anchor, the duty crew noted that the cover of the hawse pipe of the starboard anchor was opened. After informing the 2nd officer, the general alarm, including the typhoon alarm was raised. A search was conducted with no perpetrators found on board. Subsequently, the master ordered an inventory and inspection of the deck equipment. The crew were not injured. Some ship property/stores were stolen.  

The incident was reported to VTMS Corregidor and Coast Guard Station (CGS) Manila. CGS Manila immediately directed the duty MARPAT team to verify the incident, and advised the Master to strengthen onboard security measures and increase roving duties to prevent similar incidents.

While at anchor, a crew member was confronted by six perpetrators, reportedly armed with knives, at Bay 02 on the forward part of the ship. He was threatened, ordered to remain silent, and confined in the bosun store located beneath the forward mooring station. The crew member later freed himself and activated the fire alarm. The perpetrators briefly returned but were unable to gain entry, and subsequently escaped from the ship via the deck leading overboard.

An immediate search of the vessel was conducted, with no perpetrators found onboard. Subsequent investigation by the ship’s crew revealed that the padlock and securing arrangement of the bosun store door had been tampered with, indicating forced entry. The stern access to the engineer’s passageway was also found to have been tampered with. A walkie-talkie and two hydrant caps were reported stolen.

The company was notified, and the incident was reported to the local coast guard and customs authorities through the local agent.

While at anchor, the crew noticed that several items, namely cable wires and parts of the ship's beam, were missing from the ship. The master subsequently confirmed that no other losses or damages were sustained, and that no further assistance was required. The crew were not injured.

Upon receipt of the report, Coast Guard Station (CGS) Manila immediately directed Coast Guard Sub-Station (CGSS) Cavite City to conduct maritime patrol (MARPAT) operations and establish contact with the ship. Thereafter, all CGSS within the Cavite area were directed to conduct shore patrols and maintain heightened vigilance, particularly for possible sightings or recovery of the stolen items.

While at anchor, a seaborne patrol personnel of Coast Guard Sub-Station (CGSS) Bauan saw one of the perpetrators climbing the ship from an unnamed motor banca. The Philippine Coast Guard team immediately apprehended the perpetrator, and found a knife onboard the motor banca.

A comprehensive search of the ship was conducted by the combined teams of CGSS Bauan and Special Operations Group Southern Tagalog. Three additional perpetrators were found onboard the ship, and all four perpetrators were turned over to the Investigation and Detection Unit - Southern Tagalog. Nothing was stolen.

All crew members were accounted for and without injury. Some scrap metals were stolen.

Republic of Singapore Navy (RSN) and Singapore Police Coast Guard (PCG) were notified of the incident. Information of the incident was also shared with Indonesian Authority.

All crew members were accounted for and without injury. Some scrap metals were stolen.

While at anchor, several firefighting equipment and shipboard fittings were found missing from the open deck areas during a safety security round of the ship. It is believed that perpetrators boarded the ship during night time and stole the items.
 
The incident was reported to the company, local agents, and Vessel Traffic Management System (VTMS) Batangas. Additional security rounds were implemented, and all remaining bronze were removed from the open deck and secured on board as a preventive measure.

Coast Guard Station (CGS) Batangas directed Coast Guard Sub-Station (CGSS) Bauan and CGSS Mabini to intensify seaborne patrols and conduct periodic radio announcements to all nearby ships in anchorage area to remain vigilant against illegal activities.

While underway, approximately six perpetrators were sighted onboard the barge with three sampans alongside. At 1410 hrs, the master updated that the perpetrators escaped from the barge, and all three sampans departed from the area. Some scrap metals were reported stolen. The tug boat and barge continued their voyage and no assistance was required. All crew members were accounted for and without injury.

The master reported the incident to Singapore Vessel Traffic Information System (VTIS). Safety broadcasts on anti-piracy watch were initiated to remind all vessels to maintain vigilance.

While at anchor, perpetrators from one motor banca boarded the ship and stole some cables.

The incident was reported to Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) Substation Bauan. The PCG apprehended one perpetrator onboard the motor banca and conducted comprehensive search onboard and apprehended another four perpetrators. The perpetrators were charged under Violation of Article 122 of the revised Penal Code as Amended by R.A 7659- Piracy in General and Mutiny on the High Seas or in Philippine waters.
